components: a short bar that rises a little to the right
a vertical that turns and runs right along the base
strokeOrder: draw the short bar from left to right, rising a little
lift, draw the vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and run right along the base
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 030d2 file records ヒ as two stroke paths in this order and direction: the short bar, then the vertical that turns along the base; so there is one pen lift.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/030d2.svg, katakana ヒ (U+30D2 KATAKANA LETTER HI), two stroke paths kvg:030d2-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the short bar drawn left to right, rising a little; s2 starts at the top of the vertical, runs down, turns at the foot and runs right along the base. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In KanjiVG the bar starts a little to the right of the vertical; in the print glyph it starts on the vertical, so the path does too.

notes: Third sign of コーヒー.
